topic: A 73-year-old Long Island grandma, a retired 911 dispatcher, plays along with a grandparent scam and gets the fake bail bondsman arrested on her lawn
title: Scammers Wanted $8,000 From This Grandma. She Had Other Plans #truestory
case_tag: TRUE STORY · Jan 2022 · Long Island, NY
description:
#truestory #scam #grandparentscam

"Bored grandma, one. Bad guy, zero."

A fake grandson in jail, a fake lawyer, a fake bail bondsman. Jean, 73, spent 20 years as a 911 dispatcher, so she played along and handed the guy an envelope full of paper towels. The cops were waiting.

If you get a call like this, hang up and call your grandkid yourself.

#mayorofmainst #truestory #scamalert

Source: WABC, WNBC, WLNY, Fox News (Jan 2022)

Retold with AI voice & visuals
fact_notes: ABC7/WABC 2022-01 (Seaford, N.Y.): 73-year-old woman from Seaford, Long Island, asked to be identified by first name Jean; Thursday afternoon call from a man claiming to be her grandson; former 911 dispatcher; police arrested him for drunk driving, in jail; 'He started calling me grandma, and I don't have a grandson who drives, so I knew it was a scam' (WCBS); played along; after several calls a person claiming to be grandson's lawyer said $8,000 for bail; Jean contacted police, officers told her to play along; fake bail bondsman said he was in the neighborhood and could stop by to pick up cash; 'I told him I had the money in the house, and I figure he's not going to fall for that. Well, he fell for it. Hook, line and sinker.'; envelope stuffed with paper towels; as he walked away officers pounced and arrested him, 28-year-old; third-degree attempted grand larceny; 'so many people fall for this and you only hear about it on the other end after they've lost $8,000'. Oxygen (citing WNBC, WLNY, WABC, Nassau PD release): grandson caller said in jail after a car accident, charged with DUI; 'He starts calling me grandma, and then I'm like, I don't have a grandson that drives'; 'I played stupid grandma. Oh my poor grandson, please don't tell his mother'; after the lawyer call she called 911; Nassau County 911 dispatcher for more than 20 years (WNBC); officers were already at her house interviewing her about the first two calls when the third call (bail bondsman) came in; 'Apparently they thought they had the big fish. They actually thought I was gonna give them money.'; officers told her to play along, she gave her address; tackled on her front yard, caught on her Ring doorbell camera; 'Bored grandma: one. Bad guy: zero.' (WNBC); son told her 'stop, stop'; police ask residents to call police first rather than set up scammers themselves; released on appearance ticket. Fox News (Fox & Friends): son 'hang up ma', 'you're 40 years old I'm 73 and you're telling me to hang up?'. Not named on purpose: Jean asked for first name only; the man is only charged, so no name on screen. Paraphrased (not verbatim): the three scam callers' lines, built from what police and Jean said they told her. Assumed: looks, house interior, grandkid photo, the outro picture.
